record_type_quote: In our replication study, first year university students in a major university in Bangkok studied vocabulary in one of three modes.

targets.title: Second language vocabulary learning: The role of context versus translations as a function of proficiency.
targets.evidence_quote: In particular, this involved replication of Prince’s 1996 study which has been used to authorize resort to translation to teach new words.
targets.outcome_quote: Prince found the students who had studied vocabulary in translation pairs outperformed those who studied vocabulary in context in every comparison between the two modes of study. Often that difference was statistically significant. That was not the case in the present study. We found that participants who studied words in context outperformed those who studied via translation pairs.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central translation superiority result is explicitly contradicted; other Prince contrasts also did not replicate. The printed reference supplies a doi.org short alias fn5zs4 rather than an explicit DOI identifier, so doi is empty.

reasoning: The methods and conclusion identify Prince (1996) as the retested study. Other studies supply background and context or corroborating evidence, rather than independent replication targets.
